Tables with a user_id column → auto-owner-scoped. Caller only sees own rows.

app.yaml groups: { table, key, user_field } → org-scoped via membership table. The tenant clause bounds EVERYTHING on a group-keyed table: owner rows, owner_or_role tiers, member-of membership and record-level ACL grants (a share never reaches a user in another tenant).

role=admin → sees everything (override per-table via roles: scope map). EXCEPT a stepped-in admin (see api({at:'act-as'})), which deliberately drops the bypass and applies group scoping for the duration of step-in.

app.yaml scopes.<table>.public_read_when: 'status = ''published''' → matching rows become readable by every SIGNED-IN user, not only their owner (owners keep all their own rows). It does not admit anonymous visitors: they get 401 unless access.<table>.read is `anon`, and `read: anon` / `read: everyone` drop the row filter altogether, so every row (drafts included) is readable and public_read_when has no effect. To show visitors only the published rows, keep the table's read mode private and serve that slice from a public flow whose SQL carries the WHERE (api({at:'flows'})). `public_read_when` is the only key of a `scopes:` entry; any other key there is not read, and a write of app.yaml and `benmore check` warn about it.

Auto-CRUD never takes `user_id`, `role`, `password_hash`, `created_at`, `updated_at` or the groups key from a request body: the value is dropped and the `X-Stripped-Fields` response header names the column (a PATCH also lists it in `stripped_fields`). A PATCH that sends nothing else answers 400 `No fields to update` with a `hint`. Set such a column server-side, in a flow. `benmore check` warns about an app column named `role` or `password_hash`, since a client can never write it.
